messages:
anna_ml: Quick bring-up notes for axial-emb-v1 on staging. Ran the standard holdout + shortquery probe. Baseline (heron-v2 float32) r@1=0.72 r@10=0.91 silhouette=0.08. axial-emb-v1 float32 r@1=0.65 r@10=0.90 silhouette=0.03 — cluster tightness collapsed on some topical cohorts.

ben_s: Oof. What quant/serialization did you test? int8 or just fp32?

anna_ml: Both. fp32 first (the numbers above). Then ONNX int8 post-training quant. int8 r@1 drops to 0.62, r@10 ~0.88. Not catastrophic at r@10 but short queries and exact-match anchors lost a bunch.

rachel_k: Can you paste the eval command + dataset split you used? Want to reproduce quickly.

anna_ml: Sure — command and a tiny excerpt of the output:
```bash
./eval_embeddings.py --model axial-emb-v1 --split holdout_small --k 10 --batch 256 
# output snippet
# recall@1: 0.6503
# recall@10: 0.9001
# silhouette: 0.030
```
Dataset: holdout_small = 20k queries from productFAQ + 5k shorttail queries (len <= 16 chars).

uli: The silhouette drop suggests intra-cluster distances increased or inter-cluster decreased. Did you check nearest-neighbor id flips for anchors? Any examples?

anna_ml: Yep. Example where anchor id A had NN B in baseline but axial returns C (semantically less similar). Id flip list small but concentrated in short queries.

ben_s: Two quick experiments: 1) try per-channel quantization (PCQ) instead of naive per-tensor. 2) switch quant backend to symmetric with zero_point folding — we've seen better anchor retention on other models.

anna_ml: Will run both. Also adding a run where we apply L2 normalization post-quant (sometimes fixes scale drift).

devbot: @anna_ml started job embed-eval/axial-embed-perchannel-175901 at 1759013620

ci-bot: embed-eval/axial-embed-perchannel-175901 finished: summary -> r@1=0.64 r@10=0.895 silhouette=0.045 (per-channel + symmetric) — slight improvement on shorttail anchors. Link: https://ci.internal/reports/1759013620

rachel_k: Can we add the shorttail-specific microbench (k=1 k=5 only) to the weekly bakeoff to track this? Looks like axial improves r@10 but hurts r@1 which matters for some retrieval flows.

uli: Also check tokenizer normalization (accent folding / punctuation) between heron and axial training data. Small text prep mismatches can amplify after quant.

ben_s: If per-channel still not enough, try small QAT run with 1e-5 lr and dropout=0.1 on a subset (2M examples) — we got similar anchor recovery on phoenix-embed last quarter.

anna_ml: Plan: 1) run PCQ asymmetric + L2 norm (in flight), 2) schedule QAT low-lr probe (if PCQ doesn't hit target), 3) add shorttail microbench to bakeoff. Reverting prod pin to heron-v2 until parity. Thanks all :thumbsup:

devbot: Reminder created: ticket ML-1824 "axial-emb-v1 quant recovery and shorttail bakeoff" assigned to anna_ml

anna_ml: Filing follow-up notes in the model-onboard doc and will post the evaluation notebook link when done.
